people.name: Virginia Jin
people.bio: USDA-ARS research soil scientist based with the Department of Agronomy and Horticulture at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Trained in biology, forest resources and plant biology (Ph.D., University of Georgia); studies how tillage, fertilizer, irrigation and residue management shape soil carbon, microbial processes and greenhouse gas emissions.
people.research_interests: soil microbial ecology; carbon and nutrient cycling in agroecosystems; management effects on soil carbon storage and greenhouse gas emissions; agricultural mitigation of climate change

people.name: Marty R. Schmer
people.bio: Research agronomist with USDA-ARS in Lincoln, Nebraska, holding an adjunct assistant professorship in UNL's Department of Agronomy and Horticulture. Research covers sustainable and site-specific cropping systems, cellulosic bioenergy feedstocks and life-cycle assessment.
people.research_interests: site-specific crop management; sustainable cropping systems; cellulosic biofuels; life-cycle analysis

people.name: Tala Awada
people.bio: Professor of plant ecophysiology in UNL's School of Natural Resources and associate dean in the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources' Agricultural Research Division (listed as its interim dean and director). Co-leads the Platte River-High Plains Aquifer LTAR site; studies resilience of cropland, grassland and forest systems to climate and management.
people.research_interests: agroecosystem, grassland and forest sustainability and resilience; climate variability; land management effects

people.name: Andrew E. Suyker
people.bio: Micrometeorologist and research professor (associate professor rank) in UNL's School of Natural Resources. Measures carbon dioxide, water vapor and energy exchange at three cropland research sites near Mead, Nebraska, and supplies those flux records to a national archive and to other researchers.
people.research_interests: CO2 and water vapor exchange in agricultural and natural ecosystems; variability of net ecosystem exchange and evapotranspiration in irrigated and rainfed maize-soybean systems

people.name: Audrey Gamble
people.bio: Associate professor in Auburn University's Department of Crop, Soil and Environmental Sciences, specializing in soil fertility and soil conservation.

people.name: Andrew J. Margenot
people.bio: Soil scientist and faculty member in Crop Sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he is associate director of the Agroecosystem Sustainability Center and a senior associate editor of Geoderma. Earned his doctorate and held a postdoc at UC Davis before joining Illinois in 2017.
people.research_interests: soil science; FTIR spectroscopy; soil fertility in East Africa; urban agriculture; phosphorus; soil organic matter and enzymes

people.name: Maria Janowiak
people.bio: Director of both the USDA Northern Forests Climate Hub and NIACS (Northern Institute of Applied Climate Science), partnerships led by the Forest Service Northern Research Station. Helps forest managers in the Midwest and Northeast adapt to climate change through vulnerability assessments, decision tools and the Adaptive Silviculture for Climate Change trials.
people.research_interests: forests; carbon; climate adaptation planning and implementation

people.name: (Patricia) Danielle Shannon
people.bio: Serves as Northern Forests Climate Hub coordinator (USDA) and is research staff at Michigan Technological University and NIACS. Provides climate adaptation support to land managers in the Midwest and Northeast, with emphasis on forest hydrology, wetlands and forested watersheds.
people.research_interests: forest and water resources management; climate adaptation; science communication and outreach

people.name: Jessica Halofsky
people.bio: Ecologist who directs the USDA Northwest Climate Hub and the Western Wildland Environmental Threat Assessment Center (USFS Pacific Northwest Research Station); a University of Washington scientist since 2008. Has co-led many regional climate vulnerability and adaptation assessments in the western U.S.
people.research_interests: climate change impacts and adaptation; vegetation dynamics; fire and disturbance ecology

people.name: Holly R. Prendeville
people.bio: Coordinator of the USDA Northwest Climate Hub since 2016 and of the Western Wildland Environmental Threat Assessment Center. Earlier worked as a Forest Service research geneticist testing bluebunch wheatgrass seed zones for restoration; Ph.D. in ecology, evolution and behavior from UNL.
people.research_interests: restoration with native plant materials; genetics; plant evolutionary ecology

people.name: David L. Peterson
people.bio: Emeritus senior research scientist, Forest Service PNW Research Station, who also holds a University of Washington forest biology professorship. Long research record in fire science and climate change in the western U.S.; was a co-lead of the Fourth National Climate Assessment's forests chapter.
people.research_interests: fire science; climate change assessment and adaptation on western federal lands
